comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body:
Here's my crytics  
1) make juicy dynamic camera. This is what separates a cheap student's project from a serious devotion. Take inspiration from Raid movie  
2) make ragdolls stay for long. Most machines can easily handle 20-30 ragdolls lying on a ground. Exanima, Blade and Sorcery, Garry's mod - decade old games shows, that you can keep ragdols in memory  
3) take multiple animations from mixamo and blend them. With a randomized ratio. This is easy and quick to implement, and makes your game more vivid  
4) maybe implement active ragdolls on death. Falling enemy should put their hand on liver/neck/crotch, then fall, then relax unconscious. Maybe roll or crawl a little before passing out. Remeber, you don't instakill the guys. You give them pain untill they lost consciousness. 

For a future, try implementing the "enemy discombobulated, falls as a ragdoll, then stands up and continues fighting". This one is a complex problem, but people would respect you for that. And it opens big possibilities for game design

replies.author: FilipeDM
replies.body:
1- Now, when the last enemy in an area is eliminated, the camera performs a strategic close-up, highlighting their fall in slow motion.

2- Defeated enemies remain on the ground for 15 seconds before disappearing; the game continues to spawn more enemies as usual.

3- The game already includes various animations, such as left and right punches, taking damage on the left and right sides, falling to the right and left, etc.

4- I don't know how to work with ragdoll animations yet. I can't even really use Blender properly.
